 93,997 Range Rovers Recalled—Water Can Pool Around the Backup Camera and Wreck It
 A current-generation Land Rover Range Rover. Image Credit: Damian B Oh via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) 
 By: 
 Alex Harrington 
 Published: 
 October 25, 2026 - 12:17 am 
 Alex Harrington 
 October 25, 2026 
 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source 
 Land Rover is recalling 93,997 Range Rovers from the 2022 to 2026 model years because water can collect around the rearview camera and damage it.
 The tailgate trim doesn’t have enough drain holes, so water can’t drain away from the camera, according to the recall filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration . If the camera is damaged, the backup image may not show up on the screen.
 A Blank Screen in Reverse
 That’s more than an annoyance. A rearview camera that doesn’t display reduces the driver’s view behind the vehicle, which increases the risk of a crash, NHTSA says. Backup cameras have been required on every new car sold in the US since May 2018.
 NHTSA’s listing only covers the full-size Range Rover, not the Range Rover Sport or Velar.
 The Range Rover’s tailgate, home of the rearview camera. Image Credit: Aos.1905 via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) 
 What Owners Should Do
 Dealers will drill extra drain holes in the underside of the tailgate trim, then inspect the camera and replace it if it’s damaged. Repairs are free.
 The full fix isn’t ready yet. Land Rover will mail interim letters warning owners about the problem starting Dec. 11, 2026, then send a second letter once the final remedy is available.
 Owners can call Land Rover customer service at 800-637-6837 and ask about recall D171. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V678000, and owners can check their VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls .
 It’s the second Range Rover recall this month. Earlier in October, Land Rover recalled the Range Rover Sport SV over possible rear subframe cracks .
 It was a busy week for recalls overall. Porsche told owners of 548 high-performance models to park their cars because their center-lock wheel bolts can fracture, and Ford recalled 102,159 F-Series trucks over speedometers that can freeze.
